# A block carrying both spellings, naming two different transactions.
#
# `txn_guid:` names the two-line wire; the `Transaction` directive names the
# single parked CAD split. Where a block carries both, the directive decides
# and the two keys are not read — a strict override rather than a refusal,
# because someone correcting an exported block adds the advanced form to it,
# and having to delete two keys first earns nothing.
#
# **And the run says so.** The keys being read by nothing is exactly the state
# a reader cannot see in the book afterwards: nothing distinguishes "the key
# was ignored" from "the file only ever named one", so the note is the only
# thing that can. That makes it the one behaviour here where a silent
# regression would be invisible.
#
# What this fixture produces: the split named by the `Transaction` block
# settles the invoice, the transaction `txn_guid:` names is untouched, and the
# run notes that the keys went unread.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
invoice "INV-USD-001"
  customer_id: "C-US"
  currency: USD
  date_opened: 2026-01-05
  entry:
    date: 2026-01-05
    description: "Consulting"
    action: "Hours"
    account: "Income:Sales"
    quantity: 1
    price: 100
    taxable: false
    tax_included: false
  posted:
    date: 2026-01-05
    due: 2026-02-05
    ar_account: "Assets:Accounts Receivable USD"
    memo: "Invoice INV-USD-001"
    accumulate: true
  payment:
    date: 2026-02-27
    amount: 100
    account: "Assets:Bank:USD"
    txn_guid: "5e6f708192a3b4c5d6e7f80912233445"
    txn_split_guid: "708192a3b4c5d6e7f809122334455667"
    Transaction "0102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f10"
      PaymentSplit "102030405060708090a0b0c0d0e0f101"
